SELECTED_INDEX: 1
CONFIDENCE: 0.37
EXPLANATION:  The spectrum is characteristic of a small aliphatic alcohol/ether.  
• Very strong C-H stretches at 2883, 2935 and 2980 cm⁻¹ are typical of CH₃ / CH₂ groups in saturated chains (rule GFQ-003).  
• A strong band at 1091 cm⁻¹ matches the C–O stretch of an aliphatic alcohol/ether.  
• The 863 cm⁻¹ band corresponds to the C-C-O skeletal mode seen in ethanol-type fragments, while the 902 and 928 cm⁻¹ bands are additional C-C-O / C-O-C deformations that appear when an ether linkage is present.  
• 1247 cm⁻¹ (C-O stretch/CH₂ wag), 1348 cm⁻¹ (CH₃ twist) and 1458 cm⁻¹ (CH₂/CH₃ scissoring) complete the typical fingerprint set for 2-ethoxyethanol.  
Among the candidates, molecule 1 (CCOCCO, i.e. HO-CH₂-CH₂-O-CH₂-CH₃) contains exactly one ether bond and one hydroxyl group attached to a short saturated chain, giving the expected pattern of three C-C-O/C-O-C bands plus the observed alcohol/alkyl features. The other candidates either lack an ether (2, 6), contain heteroatoms expected to introduce additional distinctive bands (3 – C=S, 5 – N=O, 7 – C-F, 8 – aromatic ring, 10 – tertiary amine), or have a longer/more substituted chain that would add further peaks (4, 9). Therefore candidate 1 provides the best overall match to the experimental Raman peaks.
